translated_text:
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is Magetan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Magetan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magetan.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
5. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
6. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.
7. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
8. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
9. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
10. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to engage in business/enterprise and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Accompaniment is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and children victims of violence during the service and empowerment process.
14. Counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced;
15. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the Region that carry out integrated service functions for women and children victims of crime and/or violence, including as a center for information on women's empowerment and child protection.
16. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is one form of UPT established by the Regional Government that functions as an information center, service center and empowerment center for women and children. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.
18. Household is family members and relatives including among others grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and non-relatives including among others housemaids and drivers who live and eat from 1 (one) kitchen and reside in 1 (one) house.

text:
I. UMUM
Tindak kekerasan terhadap perempuan dan anak merupakan pelanggaran hak asasi manusia sehingga perempuan dan anak perlu dilindungi harga diri dan martabatnya serta dljamin hak hidupnya sesuai dengan frtrah dan kodratnya tanpa. diskriminasi.
Kekerasan terhadap perempuan dan anak tidak saja menimbulkan dampak lisik melainkan juga dampak psikologis yang secara umum dapat mempengaruhi kualitas hidup perempuan dan anak korban kekerasan.
Dalam skala nasional, Pemerintah Indonesia telah menandatangani Deklarasi Umum Hak Asasi Manusia (DUHAM 1948) dan meratilikasi CEDAW (Undang-Undang Nomor 7 Tahun 1948 tentang Penghapusan Segala Bentuk Distaiminasi terhadap Perempuan). Di samping itu Pemerintah juga telah mengundangkan Undang-Undang Nomor 23 Tahun 2OO2 tentarrg Perlindungan Anak sebagaimana diubah dengan Undang Undang Nomor 35 Tahun 2014 tentang Perubahan Atas Undang-Undang Nomor 23 Tahun 2002 tentang Perlindungan Anak (Lrmbaran Negara Republik Indonesia Republik Indonesia Tahun 2014 Nomor 297, Tambahan kmbaran Negara Republik Indonesia Republik Indonesia Nomor 5606) dan Undang-Undang Nomor 23 Tahun 2004 tentang Penghapusan Kekerasan Dalam Rumah Tangga (Lembaran Negara Republik Indonesia Republik Indonesia Tahun 2OO4 Nomor 95, Tambahan lembaran Negara Republik Indonesia Republik Indonesia Nomor 4419).
Selanjutnya berdasarkan Undang-Undang Nomor 23 Talnn 2OO2 tentang Perlindungan Anak sebagaimana diubah dengan Undang-Undang Nomor 35 Tahun 2014 dan Undang-Undang Nomor 23 Tahun 2014 tentang Pemerintahan Daerah sebagaimana telah diubah beberapa kali terakhir dengan Undang-Undang Nomor 9 Tahun 2015, pemberdayaan perempuan dan pelindungan anak merupakan urusan pemerintahan yang wajib dilaksanakan oleh Pemerintahan Daerah.
Sebagaimana teq'adi di berbagai daerah, termasuk juga Kabupaten Magetan saat ini terjadi tedadi fenomena peningkatan terjadinya tindak kekerasan terhadap perempuan dan anak. Guna mengatasi hal tersebut diperlukan regulasi daerah yang memberikan dasar bagi pemerintah Daerah dan/atau masyarakat dalam mewujudkan perlindungan, agar korban terhindar dan terbebas dari kekerasan atau ancaman kekerasan, penyiksaan, atau perlakuan yang merendahkan derqiat dan martabat kemanusiaan.
Dalam rangka mencegah dan menanggulangi kekerasan terhadap perempuan dan anak di Kabupaten Magetan agar terhindar dari kekerasan, ancaman kekerasan, penyiksaan atau perlakuan yang merendahkan der4iat dan martabat kemanusiaan, perru dilakukan perlindungan terhadap perempuErn dan anak korban kekerasan dalam bentuk peraturan Daerah. oleh karena itu diperlukan kebliakan yang dapat menjamin perlindungan untuk membebaskan mereka dari tindakan kekerasan, serta meningkatkan kualitas hidupnya. Berdasarkan pertimbangan-pertimbangan tersebut di atas, perlu menetapkan peraturan Daerah Kabupaten Magetan tentang Perlindungan Perempuan dan Anak Korban Kekerasan.
translated_text:
I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Violence against women and children not only causes physical impact but also psychological impact which generally can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.
On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 Year 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).
Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 Year 2014 and Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times most recently by Law Number 9 Year 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.
As occurs in various regions, including also Magetan Regency, currently there is occurring a phenomenon of increasing occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. In order to address this matter, regional regulation is needed that provides a basis for Regional Government and/or society in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.
In the framework of preventing and overcoming violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so that they are prevented from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of Regional Regulation. Therefore, a policy is needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

translated_text:
Article 4
Letter a Physical violence referred to is caused by acts that result in pain, illness, or serious injury and/or result in injury, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.
Forms of physical violence include slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/grabbing by the hair, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons.
Letter b Psychological violence referred to is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
Forms of psychological violence include emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or comments that demean self-worth, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.
Letter c Sexual violence referred to is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
Letter d Neglect referred to is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
c. acts of neglecting a person within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
Letter e Exploitation referred to is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.
Letter f Other violence referred to is caused by:
a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and/or
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Huruff Pendidikan kritis untuk perempuzrn korban kekerasan merupakan upaya membangun kesadaran perempuan tentang hak-haknya.
Tujuan dilaksanakannya pendidikan kritis adalah dapat membantu keputusan dan tidak menjadi korban kekerasan berulang. Bentuk pendidikan kritis bagi perempuan korban kekerasan terdiri dari: pelatihan-pelatihan kesetaraan dan keadilan gender, pendidikan tentang kesehatan reproduksi untuk perempuan, dan pemberian pemahaman peraturan perundang-undangan di bidang perlindungan perempuan dan anak.
Huruf a Upaya pencegahan dalam keluarga dan /atau kerabat terdekat dapat dilakukan dengan memperkuat ketahanan dalam rumah tangga seperti: pengamalan nilai-niIai keagamaan, mengatur waktu rumah tangga, dan komunikasi antar anggota keluarga.
Huruf b Upaya pencegahan dalam masyarakat meliputi: menumbuhkan kepedulian lingkungan terhadap tindak kekerasan yang te{'adi di lingkungannya.
Huruf c lembaga pendidikan dapat turut serta mengupayakan pemberian hukuman yang bersifat mendidik, mengupayakan menghapus ketentuan yang tidak berpihak pada korban kekerasan.
Huruf d Cukup jelas Cukup jelas Huruf a Pelayanan pengaduan, konsultasi, dan konseling meliputi: a. identifikasi atau pencatatan awal korban; dan
b. persetujuan dilakukan tindakan (informed consent ) yaitu persetujuan tindakan kedokteran yang diberikan oleh korban atau keluarga terdekatnya setelah mendapatkan penjelasan secara lengkap mengenai tindakan kedokteran yang akan dilakukan terhadap korban tersebut.
Huruf b Pelayanan pendampingan meliputi:
a. mendampingi korban selama proses pemeriksaan dan pemulihan kesehatan;
b. mendampingi korban selama proses medicolegal, gaitu pelayanan kedokteran untuk memberikan bantuan professional yang optimal dalam memanfaatkan ilmu kedokteran untuk kepentingan penegakan hukum dan keadilan. Termasuk pelayanan medicolegal antara lain: ui.stm et reperfitm darr uistm et psikiatrikum;
c. mendampingi korban selama proses pemeriksaan di kepolisian, kejaksaan dan pengadilan;
d. memantau kepentingan dan hak-hak korban dalam proses pemeriksaan di kepolisan, kejaksaan dan pengadilan; e. menjaga privasi dan kerahasiaan korban dari semua pihak yang tidak berkepentingan, termasuk pemberitaan oleh media massa;

Letter f Critical education for women victims of violence is an effort to build women's awareness about their rights.
The purpose of implementing critical education is to help decision-making and prevent becoming a victim of repeated violence. Forms of critical education for women victims of violence consist of: training on gender equality and justice, education on reproductive health for women, and provision of understanding of laws and regulations in the field of protection of women and children.
Letter a Prevention efforts within the family and/or closest relatives can be carried out by strengthening resilience in the household such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication among family members.
Letter b Prevention efforts in the community include: fostering environmental awareness of acts of violence occurring in their environment.
Letter c Educational institutions can participate in efforts to provide educational punishment, endeavoring to eliminate provisions that do not side with victims of violence.

Sufficiently clear.

Letter a Complaint, consultation, and counseling services include:
a. identification or initial recording of victims; and
b. informed consent, namely medical action consent given by the victim or their closest family after receiving complete explanation regarding the medical action to be performed on the victim.
Letter b Accompaniment/assistance services include:
a. accompanying victims during the examination and health recovery process;
b. accompanying victims during the medicolegal process, namely medical services to provide optimal professional assistance in utilizing medical science for the purposes of law enforcement and justice. Medicolegal services include among others: visum et repertum and visum et psikiatrikum;
c. accompanying victims during the examination process at the police, prosecutor's office and court;
d. monitoring the interests and rights of victims in the examination process at the police, prosecutor's office and court;
e. maintaining the privacy and confidentiality of victims from all parties who have no interest, including coverage by mass media;
f. coordinating with other companions/assistants; and
g. providing continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.
Letter c Health services include:
a. first aid to victims;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel; and
c. referral to health services.
Letter d Social rehabilitation services are services provided by companions/assistants in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
Forms of social rehabilitation services through provision of safe houses and social support.
Social support is carried out through:
a. spiritual guidance to victims; and
b. psychological recovery of victims.
Safe House (Shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
Letter e Legal services to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding victims' rights and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to fully describe the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions/assistants, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.
Letter f Social reintegration services aim to return victims to their families and social environment.
Social reintegration services are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. District/City Government within one Regional area of East Java Province;
b. related agencies and institutions both government and non-government; and
c. village community institutions and/or local community leaders.
Letter g Economic independence services through provision of economic access are given to victims of violence, especially women victims of violence so they can be independent in running and sustaining their lives. Such economic services can be carried out by providing training that is appropriate to the skills or talents possessed by victims, so that victims can develop the skills or talents they possess when victims return to community life. In addition, PPT can provide business information as well as job vacancies related to the skills or abilities possessed by victims of violence.
